data.source_title: An Agent Based Simulation Tool for Scheduling Emergency Department Physicians
data.locator: Methods, Table 1 (site-specific settings); Methods, patient arrival input description
data.source_setting: Single 32-bed ED in a 520-bed urban Level I trauma center, Utah, United States; about 40,000 annual visits.
data.source_period: Site ED operations; observed door-to-doctor comparison covered first 10 months of 2007. Table 1 does not provide a distinct parameter-estimation period.
data.source_n: Average weekly arrivals parameter corresponds to about 40,000 annual visits; 2007 door-to-doctor sample size not reported in extract.
data.source_evidence_basis: Author-reported site-specific input supplied to the simulation, derived from average weekly counts; this is a modeled input, not a separately tabulated raw observed distribution.
data.limitations: Single older academic trauma center. Authors describe weekly arrivals as a 168-hour heterogeneous Poisson process, estimating each hour-of-week rate from average counts for that hour; no numerical 168-hour rate vector or patient-level arrival distribution is published in the extract. external_proxy_candidate; qualitative confidence: moderate as a documented comparator, low for transfer to a local hospital.

data.source_evidence_basis: Author-reported site-specific simulation input; treated as a model parameter rather than an independently presented raw-data estimate.
